feedback.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(1,\sqrt{3}).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+3} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the point $P$ lies in the first quadrant, we can determine $\theta $ by taking the arctangent:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(2,\frac{\pi }{3}).$
